citations.claim: first violating step: total energy dropped to 134.5 from ~185-190, exceeding allowance
body 1 speed spiked to 11.21 at violating step during close approach
one step before, body 1 speed was only 8.57 while pair separation was 0.55
body 0 speed also jumped, showing violent mutual acceleration in pair 0-1

counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 0.028107906228529617 to 0.01 with all bodies, G, seed and steps unchanged; finer resolution of the 0-1 pericenter removes the energy jump

explanation: Massive bodies 0 (m=13.46) and 1 (m=6.13) undergo a deep close encounter: separation 0.92 at step 16, 0.55 at step 17, 0.138 at step 18 (below softening 0.3). Substeps_in_step stays capped at 6, so leapfrog cannot resolve the rapidly spiking acceleration/velocity (speeds jump to 8.9/11.2, kinetic 693->926, potential -503->-791 in one outer step), causing a large spurious energy drop 190.5->134.5. Momentum and angular momentum stay exact, pointing to time-resolution error, confirmed because the same 18 steps with smaller dt=0.01 passes with energy constant at ~185.4.
vision_note: In steps 15 to 16 the two upper-left blue bodies move rapidly toward each other while the other bodies remain nearly stationary. In step 17 they overlap into almost a single dot and in step 18 they appear as one larger merged blob, indicating a deep close encounter or collision.
